news_drafts.headline: Lincolnshire told of £22.5m grant covering 90% of its schools high-needs deficit after £23.0m overspend
news_drafts.lead:
Government confirmed in October 2026 that Lincolnshire County Council will receive a £22.5m High Needs Stability Grant to cover 90% of its accrued deficit on the dedicated schools grant (DSG), the government grant that funds schools. The figure appears in the auditors' annual report for 2025/26 on the council's accounts, which goes to the Audit Committee on 16 November.

The council overspent the DSG by £23.0m in 2025/26. The report attributes the overspend principally to the high needs block, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities, and says this reflects a continued increase in children and young people requiring specialist educational support. The school budget deficit stood at £13.4m in 2025/26, against £2.4m in 2024/25.

The report notes that 2025/26 was the first year in which the DSG reserve was forecast to move into a negative position. It says that position was in line with the council's Medium Term Financial Strategy, which forecast a reduction in earmarked reserves. It also says the council had established arrangements to review high needs expenditure to mitigate the DSG deficit.

news_drafts.headline: Lincolnshire to bring in new special school funding bands from the autumn 2026 term
news_drafts.lead:
Lincolnshire's special schools will be funded under a new banding model from the autumn 2026 term, according to papers for the county's Schools' Forum meeting on 8 October. Banding sets the funding a school receives according to the level of need among its pupils.

The papers, an update on reforms to support for special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), say the review of the framework has been "progressed and concluded". The new model was developed with special school leaders and finance colleagues. It is meant to line funding up more closely with need, so that banding and funding "more accurately reflect need from the outset".

A key aim, the paper says, is to reduce reliance on exceptional funding arrangements, those that sit outside the standard bands. It also links the change to the long-term financial sustainability of the High Needs Block, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities. The papers give no figures for what the new model will cost or save.

news_drafts.headline: Lincolnshire schools grant overspent by £23.0m in 2025/26, pushing its reserve negative for first time
news_drafts.lead:
Lincolnshire County Council overspent its dedicated schools grant (the government grant that funds schools) by £23.0 million in 2025/26, according to a value for money risk assessment before its Audit Committee on 21 September. The year was the first in which the grant's reserve moved into a negative position.

The paper attributes the overspend principally to the high needs block, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities. It says this reflects "a continued increase in the number of children and young people requiring specialist educational support and services." The paper describes the deficit as a structural demand pressure that persists, rather than a one-year variation.

The council has set up arrangements to review how effective its high needs spending is. The paper does not give a figure for the total deficit now carried on the grant, a date by which the overspend is expected to stop, or the amount the review is expected to save.

findings.paper_title: App C - Auditors Annual Report (Lincolnshire County Council) 2025-26
findings.headline: The auditor has raised a recommendation for structured reporting against the 2026-31 Corporate Plan, after no equivalent performance reporting was presented during 2025/26
findings.detail: The paper says the Council continued to publish performance information on its website during 2025/26. It records that the auditor's review found no significant poor performance at service line or corporate level.
findings.matters: A peer council would note that performance reporting to committees is being reintroduced against the new plan, which is a governance change.
findings.quote: we have raised a recommendation that structured reporting against the Council

findings.paper_title: App C - Auditors Annual Report (Lincolnshire County Council) 2025-26
findings.headline: Finance and Payroll/HR Administration services were insourced from the Serco contract, which had run for 24 years
findings.detail: The paper describes the insourcing as part of a programme to bring previously outsourced services back in-house. It says the Council operates a relatively limited number of outsourced services.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would see this as a concrete example of a shared-services contract being brought in-house.
findings.quote: responsibility for Finance and Payroll/HR Administration services was successfully insourced

findings.paper_title: App C - Auditors Annual Report (Lincolnshire County Council) 2025-26
findings.headline: Year-end borrowings of £446.9m, down from £453.4m, and a year-end cash position of (£19.6m) against (£108.3m) the prior year
findings.detail: The paper reports these as part of its key financial and performance metrics table, without further commentary on the borrowing or cash position.
findings.matters: A lender would track year-end borrowings and the cash position as a measure of the Council's funding need.

findings.paper_title: App C - Auditors Annual Report (Lincolnshire County Council) 2025-26
findings.headline: The Government announced in October 2026 that it had withdrawn its LGR decision for Lincolnshire, with a further review likely to conclude by early 2027
findings.detail: The paper says the Council's November 2025 proposal was for a single unitary authority, and that the Government had decided on two unitaries before the later withdrawal. It notes the reorganisation timetable has been paused.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would track this as a reorganisation timetable that has moved, affecting financial planning and future value for money considerations.
findings.quote: In October 2026 the Government announced that it had withdrawn its LGR decision for Lincolnshire and a further review would take place and likely conclude by early 2027.

findings.paper_title: App C - Auditors Annual Report (Lincolnshire County Council) 2025-26
findings.headline: The CQC report on adult social care was de-published after the Council challenged its factual accuracy, and a revised report published in November 2026 gives an overall score of 'Good'
findings.detail: The paper says the original report gave a required improvement score, and the Council created an action plan before the de-publication. The paper's metrics table records the 2025-26 CQC rating as TBC, which does not match the November 2026 revised rating in the text.
findings.matters: A finance director would note that a regulator's rating was contested and reissued, and that the auditor's risk assessment relied on the original report.
findings.quote: The Council challenged the factual accuracy of the report, which was subsequently de-published by the CQC.
